package_info.package_manager: system (Linux distribution package managers: dpkg, rpm, etc.)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a sophisticated backdoor introduced via a malicious build process, which modifies the liblzma library to enable remote code execution and SSH authentication bypass on affected Linux systems. The backdoor leverages advanced techniques (e.g., glibc IFUNC, audit hooks) to intercept and replace cryptographic functions, allowing attackers to gain unauthorized access to systems using the compromised library.

execution_context.trigger: build-time (during package compilation on target system)
execution_context.file_location: build-to-host.m4 (malicious M4 macro file in tarball, not in git repo)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: M4 macro logic that extracts and injects malicious object code into the build process, targeting x86-64 Linux with glibc and GCC, and only when built via dpkg or rpm.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code checks for specific build environments (x86-64, glibc, GCC, dpkg/rpm) and conditionally extracts and injects a malicious object file into the resulting liblzma binary, enabling later runtime exploitation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The build file is present only in the tarball (not in source control), and its logic is designed to conditionally inject code only on certain systems, evading detection during normal development and review.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal build scripts should not inject hidden object code or conditionally alter binaries based on environment; this is a clear violation of expected transparent build processes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Conditional compilation for platform-specific optimizations is legitimate, but not for injecting hidden, undocumented code.
key_indicators: Presence of build-to-host.m4 only in release tarball
Conditional logic targeting specific build environments
Injection of object code not present in source repository

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when liblzma is loaded, e.g., via sshd with systemd patch)
execution_context.file_location: liblzma.so (compiled shared library, after build-time injection)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious code leveraging glibc IFUNC mechanism to add a resolver for crc64_resolve, which installs a glibc audit hook to intercept and replace the RSA_public_decrypt function in OpenSSH.
malicious_snippets.code_language: C (compiled to object code, injected via build process)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the compromised liblzma is loaded (e.g., via libsystemd in patched sshd), the code uses the glibc IFUNC resolver to install an audit hook that intercepts calls to RSA_public_decrypt, replacing it with a malicious implementation that allows authentication bypass or remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of glibc IFUNC and audit hooks to intercept cryptographic functions is highly unusual and only makes sense for malicious purposes, especially in a compression library.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Compression libraries should not interact with cryptographic functions or install audit hooks affecting unrelated system components.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Audit hooks may be used for debugging or profiling, but never for cryptographic function replacement in production libraries.
key_indicators: Replacement of RSA_public_decrypt in OpenSSH context

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a specially crafted compressed test file is processed)
execution_context.file_location: liblzma test files (maliciously crafted, embedded in package)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Maliciously crafted compressed test files that, when processed, trigger the backdoor logic in the injected code.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the malicious test file is processed by the library, it triggers the backdoor logic, activating the IFUNC resolver and audit hook installation, enabling the authentication bypass or code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Test files should not trigger hidden code paths or activate backdoors; their use here is to stealthily activate malicious logic only under specific conditions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Test files are expected to validate functionality, not to serve as triggers for hidden code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this is a clear abuse of test infrastructure.
key_indicators: Test files as triggers for hidden code
Activation of backdoor logic only when specific files are processed

attack_chain.action: Malicious build-to-host.m4 file is included in the release tarball and triggers during package build on targeted systems.
attack_chain.leads_to: Injection of malicious object code into liblzma binary

attack_chain.action: Injected object code leverages glibc IFUNC to install a glibc audit hook at runtime when liblzma is loaded (e.g., via libsystemd in sshd).
attack_chain.leads_to: Interception and replacement of RSA_public_decrypt in OpenSSH

attack_chain.action: Maliciously crafted compressed test files are processed, triggering the backdoor logic in the injected code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Activation of authentication bypass or remote code execution in sshd

attack_chain.action: Attacker authenticates to the compromised SSH server using a crafted RSA key, bypassing normal authentication.
attack_chain.leads_to: Unauthorized remote access or code execution on the target system

behavioral_signatures: Presence of build scripts or files in release tarballs not present in source control
Conditional injection of object code during build targeting specific environments
Use of glibc IFUNC resolvers and audit hooks in non-cryptographic libraries
Interception or replacement of cryptographic functions (e.g., RSA_public_decrypt) by unrelated libraries
Activation of hidden code paths when processing specific test files
file_indicators: build-to-host.m4 present in tarball but not in git repository
liblzma.so binaries with unexpected object code sections
Maliciously crafted compressed test files embedded in package
network_indicators: Unusual authentication attempts to sshd from external sources
Potential exfiltration or command-and-control traffic if attacker leverages remote code execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Compare release tarballs to source repositories for unexpected files (e.g., build-to-host.m4). Analyze build logs for conditional object code injection. Inspect liblzma.so binaries for IFUNC resolvers and audit hooks. Monitor for libraries intercepting cryptographic functions. Scan for the presence of maliciously crafted test files. Monitor SSH authentication logs for unusual patterns, especially on systems with affected liblzma versions.
